Synthetic TOPIA profiles

Source: R/topia-simulate.R
topia_simulate.Rd

Generate TOPIA weather and demand profiles from a closed-form model of the map, at any resolution and for any cluster roster. The shipped "simulated" dataset (topia) is one cached run of this function, so topia_simulate() at its defaults reproduces it and every other parameter set is an alternative.

The output is shaped like topia_profiles()'s, so either can be passed to build_topia(weather = , demand = ).

Usage

topia_simulate(
  regions = NULL,
  calendar = "s4_h24",
  clusters = NULL,
  solar_season = .SIM_M_SOL,
  wind_season = .SIM_M_WIN,
  hydro_season_calm = .SIM_M_HYD_A,
  hydro_season_windy = .SIM_M_HYD_B,
  wind_day_calm = .SIM_H_WIN_CALM,
  wind_day_windy = .SIM_H_WIN_WINDY,
  load_day_res = .SIM_H_RES,
  load_day_ind = .SIM_H_IND,
  load_season_res = .SIM_M_RES,
  load_season_ind = .SIM_M_IND,
  residential = .SIM_W_RES,
  wind_grade = .SIM_WIN_GRADE,
  solar_halflen = .SIM_SOL_HALFLEN,
  hydro_cf = .SIM_HYD_CF,
  jitter = 0,
  seed = NULL,
  layout = "honeycomb",
  measured = NULL
)

Arguments

regions

provinces to generate, defaulting to all of TOPIA's.

calendar

a calendar name, a calendar object, or a timetable data.frame. It must carry an HOUR frame and either YDAY or SEASON above it.

clusters

the roster to generate: a data.frame of resource, cluster and region, or NULL to take the rosters the shipped weather objects declare. FALSE generates one ungraded series per resource.

solar_season, wind_season, hydro_season_calm, hydro_season_windy

twelve monthly multipliers each, normalised to mean 1 internally.

wind_day_calm, wind_day_windy, load_day_res, load_day_ind

twenty-four hourly values each: the endpoints the shapes are blended between.

load_season_res, load_season_ind

twelve monthly multipliers each.

residential

residential share of load by zone, named.

wind_grade, solar_halflen

the cluster shape parameters, named by cluster.

hydro_cf

annual mean inflow factor, used where the measured set has no hydro series for a province.

jitter

relative amplitude of a deterministic perturbation applied to each field, 0 for none. The mean is preserved and no values are made equal, so the energy is unbiased and the LP stays non-degenerate.

seed

integer seed for jitter.

layout

the geoscale whose zones the load mix is keyed on.

measured

the measured frames the levels are calibrated against, as list(weather =, demand =). NULL reads the shipped set, which is what a user wants; the dataset build passes its own frames, since at that point the shipped set is what is being written.

Value

a list of two tidy data.frames: weather (resource, cluster, region, timeslice, wval) and demand (region, timeslice, load), both carrying a dataset attribute naming the generator and the parameters that differ from the defaults.

Details

Levels are calibrated against the shipped measured set: each (resource, cluster, province) field is scaled to the mean capacity factor measured there, and the load shape to the measured peak-to-mean. What the arguments change is the SHAPE.

Clusters differ through one parameter each – wind_grade offsets a grade along the calm-to-windy axis, solar_halflen sets the half-length of the solar day per mounting – so a grade is a different resource rather than another ceiling on one series. A roster with no clusters yields one series per resource with cluster NA, which no graded technology can use; see build_topia(clusters = ).

See also

topia_profiles() for the shipped sets, build_topia(), topia_profile() for geometric shapes

Other topia: topia, topia_profile(), topia_profiles()

Examples

p <- topia_simulate(regions = c("R01", "R10"), calendar = "s4_h24")
head(p$weather, 3)
#>   resource cluster region timeslice wval
#> 1     WSOL      FL    R01   WIN_h00    0
#> 2     WSOL      FL    R01   WIN_h01    0
#> 3     WSOL      FL    R01   WIN_h02    0

# an alternative: no seasonality in the wind
p2 <- topia_simulate(regions = c("R01", "R10"), wind_season = rep(1, 12))
